title: 4 Days Body Part split Review
summary: He reviews viewer Kobe's 4-day barbell-based body-part/lift split (deadlift-back, bench-OHP, squat-legs, close-grip-arms). He mostly approves, but replaces 5x5 back-off sets with 3x5 on the main lifts, cuts the double row work, wants more back-off volume on OHP, and advises losing weight before chasing a 3-plate bench.

claims.claim: For an overweight lifter, waiting to hit a strength goal (e.g. a 3-plate bench) before losing weight is a poor priority: you'll lose the lift as you cut, which hurts psychologically. Better to lose fat while gaining strength and hit the number at a lower bodyweight.
He got his own 3-plate bench while bulking.
The deadlift tolerates low frequency or a single heavy set per session, because the long ramp of warm-ups needed for such heavy loads already adds decent tonnage.

A 5x5 back-off after an AMRAP top set forces submaximal weight: either set 1 is too easy and you left strength in the tank, or you strain to get set 5. A 3x5 back-off fits better and progresses more easily.
Holding the barbell after the last deadlift rep trains grip, and also the traps if you let the weight stretch them.
He always advises a pronated grip for barbell rows, and thinks barbell rows suit higher rep ranges (12-15) rather than pushing intensity.

Doing pronated and supinated barbell rows on the same day is too much volume and not quality tonnage; do one (then 4x8-12 to push weight), alternate them across sessions, or swap one for inverted rows.
Rear-delt raises at 4x12-15 is a good rep range for shoulders and fine after pulls, once the shoulders are warm.
Don't superset AMRAP or 3x5 strength work; barbell rows can be supersetted with rear-delt raises.
Inverted rows are very challenging for overweight lifters and stimulate the back well.
Building each day around a body part linked to a main lift is a smart way to programme.

Horizontal presses need more volume to progress the bench, which is why 5x5 back-offs suit the bench better than other lifts; still, he suggests AMRAP plus 3x5 paused, then focusing on a medium-grip bench or decline push-ups to see if it carries over.
He doesn't use rep ranges for calisthenics and always does as many reps as possible, since calisthenics doesn't burn you out; all-out pull-ups won't hurt lifting the same or next day.
A single AMRAP set is not enough OHP volume; add back-off work (3x5), or try a set of 5 at lighter weight followed by heavier sets of 1-2 to manipulate intensity.
He always promotes OHP on the same day as bench: it helps shoulder health and takes less from your strength than people think.
Side raises at 4x12-15 are good on a pressing day.
If the triceps aren't responding to bench, add long-head and medial-head work; no supersets on a day with three sets of strength-type pressing, since they'd cut into the strength work.
Deadlifting on Monday means legs are hit twice a week, avoiding the trap of training legs only once.
Single-leg calf raises at 4x12-15 with slow negatives are a lot of work for an overweight person carrying extra mass.
Step-ups (4x6-8 per leg) plus single-leg dumbbell RDLs (4x8-12) give a good quad/hamstring balance; step-ups also hit the glutes and hamstrings.
Like the deadlift, the squat can get away with low frequency or volume for some people; if you're progressing, keep going.
Close-grip bench is a good bench-builder: it adds horizontal pressing volume, spares the shoulders, and carries over to the regular bench in both directions.
Two to three days between chest sessions is enough recovery for most people.
Lying triceps extensions behind the head work the long head; 4x8-12 is a good range.
Biceps trained once a week is low frequency, but a top set of 8-10 plus 4x8-12 back-offs is enough volume to make it work.
Towel hammer curls with a plate attached are a great lift for the forearms and arms; he does them for 4 sets of 6-10.
AMRAP plus 5x5 suits the close-grip bench better than the regular bench, because as a variation you're pushing intensity rather than progression as aggressively.
Whether to finish an arm day with a heavy curl or a lighter isolation lift depends on the person; try supersetting triceps extensions with towel hammer curls and finishing on barbell curls.
He doesn't squat often because of his knees.

exercises.name: Deadlift (AMRAP + back-off)
cues: 1-5 hard reps then 3x5 back-off instead of 5x5
hold the bar after the last rep for grip/traps
exercises.why: submaximal 5x5 either leaves strength in the tank or strains you

exercises.name: Pronated barbell row
cues: 12-15 reps, or 4x8-12 if it's the only row
exercises.why: suits higher reps, don't push intensity

exercises.name: Inverted row
exercises.why: replaces a second barbell row, hard and effective for heavier lifters

exercises.name: Overhead press
cues: needs back-off sets, not just an AMRAP
exercises.why: shoulder health, little interference with bench

exercises.name: Close-grip bench press
exercises.why: spares shoulders, carries over to bench
